business_model.claim: Ternium generates its primary revenue by manufacturing and selling steel products—including slabs, heavy plates, hot and cold rolled products, coated products, automotive stamped steel parts, roll-formed and tubular products, billets, and bars—along with other products such as energy sales.
quotes: Ternium’s primary source of revenue is the sale of steel products.

The Steel segment includes the sales of steel products done by the Company's subsidiaries, which comprises mainly slabs, heavy plates, hot and cold rolled products, coated products, stamped steel parts for the automotive industry, roll-formed and tubular products, billets, bars and other products, including sales of energy.

business_model.claim: Ternium also produces and sells mining products, mainly iron ore and iron ore pellets, both externally to third parties and intercompany.
quotes: The Mining segment includes the sales of mining products done by the Company's subsidiaries, mainly iron ore and iron ore pellets

In 2025, the Mining Segment’s net sales increased year-over-year primarily as a result of higher iron ore shipments, reflecting better volumes in both Brazilian and Mexican operations, partially offset by lower realized iron ore prices.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P3
business_model.claim: Ternium sells its steel products to manufacturing industries and the construction sector, with the construction, automotive, appliance, and machinery industries serving as significant end markets.
quotes: Ternium is a leading steel producer in the Americas, providing advanced steel products to a broad range of manufacturing industries and the construction sector.
Steel demand is sensitive to trends in cyclical industries, such as the construction, automotive, appliance and machinery industries, which are significant markets for Ternium’s products

business_model.claim: The majority of Ternium's sales are concentrated in the Americas—primarily Mexico, Brazil, and Argentina—with net sales by customer location of 6,756,721 in Mexico, 3,108,167 in Brazil, 1,636,450 in the Southern region, and 1,417,224 in Other markets out of 12,918,562 total net sales (table in $ thousands), while generating no revenues in Luxembourg.
quotes: The majority of Ternium’s sales are concentrated in the Americas.
Specifically, Ternium’s largest markets are Mexico, Brazil and Argentina.
For purposes of reporting geographical information, net sales are allocated based on the customer’s location.
The Company had no revenues attributable to the Company’s country of incorporation (Luxembourg) in 2026.

business_model.claim: Ternium is organized into two reporting operating segments, Steel and Mining, overseen by its Chief Executive Officer as Chief Operating Decision Maker using management-view operating income without reviewing segment assets.
quotes: The Company is organized in two operating segments: Steel and Mining.
Ternium's Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") functions as the CODM.
Information on segment assets is not disclosed as it is not reviewed by the CEO.

business_model.claim: Revenue and operating results are sensitive to volatile steel prices—which move with steel demand and raw material costs such as scrap, iron ore, and metallurgical coal—as shown in 2025 when lower realized prices drove a 10% drop in steel revenue per ton and a 13% decline in Steel segment net sales.
quotes: Steel prices are volatile and are sensitive to trends in steel demand and raw material costs, such as steel scrap, iron ore and metallurgical coal costs.
The Steel Segment’s net sales decreased by 13% year-over-year in 2025.
Steel revenue per ton declined by 10%, reflecting lower realized steel prices across Ternium’s main steel markets.

business_model.claim: Sales volumes and revenues depend on macroeconomic activity in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and regional markets—where steel consumption historically tracks GDP and per capita disposable income—alongside customer inventory swings and supply chain disruptions.
quotes: Historically, annual steel consumption in the countries where Ternium operates has varied at a rate that is linked to the annual change in each country’s gross domestic product and per capita disposable income.

Fluctuations in steel inventory levels and disruptions in customers’ supply chains can temporarily affect the demand for, and price of, steel products and, accordingly, Ternium may not be able to increase or maintain its current levels of sales volume or prices.

business_model.claim: Global steel overcapacity—particularly in China, whose exports of semifinished and finished steel products increased from 53 million tons in 2020 to 117 million tons in 2024—together with U.S. steel import tariffs raised to 50% and USMCA trade uncertainty, pressures Ternium's demand, volumes, and margins.
quotes: China’s exports of semifinished and finished steel products increased from 53 million tons in 2020 to 117 million tons in 2024 and are estimated to have expanded further in 2025.
This expansion in Chinese exports caused a surge of low-priced steel imports in the Brazilian domestic steel market, adversely affecting Brazilian steel producers, including Usiminas.
Steel was a primary focus, with the United States revoking all country-specific exemptions to the 25% tariff on steel imports under Section 232 and raising the tariff to 50%.
Uncertainty surrounding tariff negotiations with the United States weighed on steel demand in Mexico, where apparent steel use declined by roughly 10% year-over-year in 2025.

business_model.claim: Ternium seeks to grow higher-margin revenues by focusing on sophisticated value-added products and substituting steel imports in Mexico through downstream lines and a new DRI-EAF steel slab facility at its Pesquería Industrial Center.
quotes: Three main drivers compose Ternium’s business strategy: a focus on sophisticated value-added products, the pursuit of strategic growth opportunities and a relentless quest for competitive industrial operations.
Mexico has an attractive steel market with significant demand for advanced steel products, and foreign steel producers cover approximately half of the flat steel demand in the country.

The new facilities, consisting of an electric-arc-furnace-based steel shop and a DRI module, are expected to produce the highest specification steels, necessary for the most demanding applications of the automotive industry, and to comply with USMCA's melted and poured rules of origin.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Ternium's cost structure is driven primarily by raw materials, purchased slabs, and energy (such as natural gas) bought at market or market-based prices, alongside labor and maintenance, with raw materials and consumables totaling 8,239,820 out of 10,254,080 in cost of sales (table in $ thousands).
quotes: Ternium purchases substantial quantities of raw materials (including iron ore, coal, ferroalloys and scrap) and slabs for use in the production of its steel products.
In addition to raw materials and slabs, natural gas is an important component of Ternium’s cost structure.
Raw materials and consumables used and other movements | 8,239,820 | 6,996,599

business_model.claim: Under Ternium's first-in, first-out (FIFO) inventory accounting methodology, falling raw material prices do not immediately reduce reported production costs, and Ternium may face delays or inability in passing through higher raw material and energy costs via selling prices.
quotes: Furthermore, if raw material costs decline, the resulting reduction in steel production costs would not be immediately reflected in Ternium’s operating results as we would first consume existing inventories acquired prior to such raw material cost decrease (first in - first out accounting methodology).
Similarly, we may be unable to recover, in whole or in part, increased costs of raw materials and energy through increased selling prices on steel products, or it may take considerable time to do so.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Input costs and availability are exposed to tightening global slab supply—from competitor vertical integration and sanctions on Russian steel companies—and dependence on a limited number of key suppliers such as Vale for iron ore and Petrobras for petcoke, coke, and natural gas.
quotes: Purchased slabs are a key component of Ternium’s production process.
Industry consolidation and integration of slab making facilities into finished steel products have been reducing the availability of slabs in the global market.
We depend on a limited number of key suppliers for the provision of certain key inputs.

For example, Ternium Argentina and Ternium Brasil purchase most of their iron ore from Vale, a Brazilian company, and Ternium Mexico is also expected to begin relying on steady iron ore supplies from Vale once its steelmaking facilities in Pesquería, Mexico, start operations.

business_model.claim: Ternium mitigates cost pressures through competitiveness and efficiency programs—such as blast furnace stability, iron ore sourcing optimization, logistics streamlining, service contract renegotiations, Usiminas plant upgrades, and a wind farm in Argentina that lowered energy costs.
quotes: Key initiatives that generated significant savings included enhancing blast furnace stability, optimizing iron ore sourcing, streamlining logistics, and renegotiating service contracts.
In early 2025, the company completed its investment in a new wind farm in the country, which contributed to lowering energy costs for Ternium’s operations.
Usiminas advanced several projects aimed at improving the cost structure of its steel production facilities.

business_model.claim: Costs and operating results are also affected by foreign currency movements on non-U.S. dollar transactions across USD-functional-currency subsidiaries, unionized labor negotiations and profit-sharing disputes, and geopolitical conflicts that can disrupt energy and raw material markets.
quotes: A significant portion of Ternium’s transactions is carried out in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.
Fluctuations in the value of such local currencies against the U.S. dollar have had, and may also have in the future, an impact on Ternium’s results.

A substantial majority of Ternium’s employees at its manufacturing subsidiaries are represented by labor unions and are covered by collective bargaining or similar agreements, which are subject to periodic renegotiation.
Escalation of this conflict could disrupt energy markets, increase raw material costs and impair supply chain reliability.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium is a leading steel producer in the Americas and Latin America, supplying advanced steel products to manufacturing industries and the construction sector.
quotes: Ternium is a leading steel producer in the Americas, providing advanced steel products to a broad range of manufacturing industries and the construction sector.

Ternium aims to enhance stakeholder value by further consolidating its position as a leading steel producer in Latin America and a strong player in the Americas, while increasing its differentiation and strengthening its competitiveness.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium holds significant positions across Latin America's major steel markets, with Mexico, Brazil, and Argentina as its largest markets alongside operations in Colombia and Central America.
quotes: Specifically, Ternium’s largest markets are Mexico, Brazil and Argentina.
In Brazil, the second largest steel market in Latin America, Usiminas is one of the main producers of flat steel products.
Ternium Argentina has a significant presence in the Argentine steel market, the third largest in Latin America.
In Colombia, the fourth largest steel market in Latin America, Ternium has the capacity to produce long products and to process and distribute flat and long steel products.
Other facilities with finishing lines and service centers in Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica enable Ternium to maintain a vast presence in the region.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium differentiates itself through its network of distribution centers and commercial offices, an integrated customer connectivity platform, and its ProPymes SME program in Argentina and Mexico.
quotes: Our industrial presence and network of distribution centers and commercial offices increase Ternium’s ability to offer differentiated logistics and stock management services.
In addition, our integrated connectivity platform covering the entire customer relationship process enables Ternium to provide a better and faster response to its customers’ needs.
Ternium works together with small and medium-sized customers and suppliers in Argentina and Mexico, through the ProPymes program, to help them prosper.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium integrated its Rio de Janeiro slab facility (annual capacity 5.0 million tons, lifting system crude steel capacity to 12.4 million tons in 2017) with a 4.4 million tons hot-rolling mill in Pesquería, Mexico that started up in 2021.
quotes: For example, in 2017 Ternium acquired a steel producer, renamed Ternium Brasil, with facilities located in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, with annual production capacity of 5.0 million tons of high-end steel slabs.
With this acquisition, total crude steel production capacity of Ternium’s industrial system in 2017 increased to 12.4 million tons, or by approximately 70%.

The acquisition of the Rio de Janeiro facility triggered the construction of the new hot-rolling mill in Pesquería, Mexico, with annual production capacity of 4.4 million tons which started up in 2021.
This new facility enabled the integration of the Rio de Janeiro slab facility with Ternium’s industrial system in Mexico.

competitive_position.claim: In Mexico, where foreign producers cover approximately half of flat steel demand, Ternium completed its Pesquería downstream expansion and is building a DRI-EAF slab facility expected to start operations by the fourth quarter of 2026 to serve automotive demand and comply with USMCA rules of origin.
quotes: Mexico has an attractive steel market with significant demand for advanced steel products, and foreign steel producers cover approximately half of the flat steel demand in the country.
With the commissioning of these facilities, Ternium completed its downstream expansion at the site, which also includes a pickling line and finishing facilities already in operation.
In addition, Ternium is building new steel slab-making facilities in the Pesquería Industrial Center, with operations expected to commence by the fourth quarter of 2026.

The new facilities, consisting of an electric-arc-furnace-based steel shop and a DRI module, are expected to produce the highest specification steels, necessary for the most demanding applications of the automotive industry, and to comply with USMCA's melted and poured rules of origin.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium began consolidating Usiminas in July 2023 after increasing its control-group participation to 51.5%, and in February 2026 increased that participation to 83.1% by acquiring 153.1 million ordinary shares from the NSC Group.
quotes: On July 3, 2023, Ternium Investments and Ternium Argentina, together with TenarisConfab, acquired from the NSC Group, pro rata to their then participations in the T/T Group, 68.7 million ordinary shares of Usiminas, increasing Ternium’s participation in the Usiminas control group to 51.5%.
A new shareholders’ agreement was entered into as a result of that transaction, and we began to fully consolidate Usiminas in July 2023.

On February 10, 2026, Ternium Investments acquired from the NSC Group their remainder participation in the Usiminas control group, totaling 153.1 million ordinary shares, increasing Ternium’s participation in the Usiminas control group from 51.5% to 83.1%.

Pursuant to the Usiminas shareholders agreement, Ternium Investments has the right to nominate a majority of the members of Usiminas’ board of directors, the CEO and all other members of Usiminas’ board of officers.

competitive_position.claim: Operating income declined each year from 2022 through 2025, falling 44% year-over-year in 2025 to $705 million (5% of net sales) due to lower realized steel prices and lower sales volumes.
quotes: As a result of steel price volatility, among other factors, Ternium’s operating income decreased by 44% year-over-year in 2025 after decreasing 43% year-over-year in 2024, 19% year-over-year in 2023 and 49% year-over-year in 2022, and increasing 388% year-over-year in 2021.
Operating income decreased year-over-year in 2025 to $705 million, with an operating income over net sales of 5%.

The decline in operating income reflected the drop in steel prices together with lower sales volumes, countered by the successful implementation of the competitiveness plan to cut costs and increase efficiency at our operations, as well as by lower raw material and purchased slab costs.

competitive_position.claim: In the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, consolidated net sales rose to 12,918,562 (table in $ thousands) and operating income increased to 1,396,382 (table in $ thousands), versus 11,834,309 and 546,453 in the same period of 2025, led by Mexico net sales of 6,756,721 (table in $ thousands).

Ternium supported its cost competitiveness in 2025 through efficiency initiatives—enhancing blast furnace stability, optimizing iron ore sourcing, streamlining logistics, renegotiating service contracts, completing a wind farm in Argentina, and advancing Usiminas cost projects—while financing $2.5 billion of capital expenditures largely with $2.3 billion in operating cash flow and cash on hand.
quotes: Despite these challenging dynamics, Ternium delivered resilient results by swiftly adapting to the new environment and implementing a comprehensive cost-reduction and efficiency program.
Key initiatives that generated significant savings included enhancing blast furnace stability, optimizing iron ore sourcing, streamlining logistics, and renegotiating service contracts.
In early 2025, the company completed its investment in a new wind farm in the country, which contributed to lowering energy costs for Ternium’s operations.
Usiminas advanced several projects aimed at improving the cost structure of its steel production facilities.
Capital expenditures reached $2.5 billion in the year, the peak of the current investment cycle, with the bulk allocated to the continuing expansion of the industrial center in Pesquería.
These capital outflows were largely financed through cash generated by operating activities of $2.3 billion and cash on hand.

competitive_position.claim: A surge in U.S. trade actions in 2025—including revoking country exemptions and raising the Section 232 steel import tariff from 25% to 50%—created uncertainty and contributed to an approximate 10% year-over-year fall in Mexico's apparent steel demand in 2025.
quotes: Steel was a primary focus, with the United States revoking all country-specific exemptions to the 25% tariff on steel imports under Section 232 and raising the tariff to 50%.

For example, the surge in U.S. trade action in 2025 has created significant uncertainty in global markets and has contributed to a reduction in Mexico’s apparent steel demand, which fell by approximately 10% year-over-year in 2025.
Our business could be materially and adversely affected by changes to trade regulations in the USMCA region.

competitive_position.claim: Severe overcapacity in China drove Chinese semifinished and finished steel exports from 53 million tons in 2020 to 117 million tons in 2024 (estimated higher in 2025), fueling a surge of low-priced steel imports into Brazil that pressured Usiminas' profitability.
quotes: Over the last several years, overcapacity has been particularly severe in China.
China’s exports of semifinished and finished steel products increased from 53 million tons in 2020 to 117 million tons in 2024 and are estimated to have expanded further in 2025.
This expansion in Chinese exports caused a surge of low-priced steel imports in the Brazilian domestic steel market, adversely affecting Brazilian steel producers, including Usiminas.
In Brazil, the influx of low-priced Chinese steel products continued to pressure Usiminas’ profitability.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium faces intense competition on price, quality, and service from steelmakers that may possess greater resources or government support and are consolidating, as well as competition from alternative materials including aluminum, wood, concrete, plastic, and ceramics.
quotes: In both global and regional markets, Ternium competes against other global and local producers of steel products, which in some cases have greater financial and operating resources or direct and indirect governmental support.
In addition, there has been a trend toward steel industry consolidation among competitors, and current competitors in the steel market could become larger competitors in the future.
Moreover, Ternium and other steelmakers compete against suppliers of alternative materials, including aluminum, wood, concrete, plastic and ceramics.

competitive_position.claim: Purchased slabs are a key input for Ternium, and global slab availability is shrinking due to competitor vertical integration—such as ArcelorMittal integrating Lázaro Cárdenas and acquiring Brazilian slab maker CSP in 2023—alongside trade sanctions linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
quotes: Purchased slabs are a key component of Ternium’s production process.
Industry consolidation and integration of slab making facilities into finished steel products have been reducing the availability of slabs in the global market.
For example, ArcelorMittal gradually integrated its slab facility in Lázaro Cárdenas, Mexico, with its steel processing facilities in other locations.
Furthermore, in 2023 it acquired Companhia Siderúrgica do Pecém (CSP), a Brazilian slab maker that used to be a significant supplier of slabs in the international markets.

New international sanctions against Russian steel companies or citizens could result in slab scarcity and/or increases in slab prices in the market, which could have a material adverse effect on Ternium’s business and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Ternium relies on a limited number of key suppliers, with Ternium Argentina and Ternium Brasil sourcing most of their iron ore from Vale and Ternium Mexico expected to rely on Vale once Pesquería steelmaking starts.
quotes: We depend on a limited number of key suppliers for the provision of certain key inputs.

For example, Ternium Argentina and Ternium Brasil purchase most of their iron ore from Vale, a Brazilian company, and Ternium Mexico is also expected to begin relying on steady iron ore supplies from Vale once its steelmaking facilities in Pesquería, Mexico, start operations.

competitive_position.claim: Steel price volatility—illustrated by U.S. hot-rolled coil prices swinging from $485 per ton in 2020 to $2,135 per ton in 2021—combined with FIFO inventory accounting and geopolitical conflicts such as Iran-U.S.-Israel tensions can delay cost reductions or prevent pass-through of higher input and energy costs.
quotes: For instance, U.S. prices of hot-rolled coils bottomed in 2020 at $485 per ton, peaked at $2,135 per ton in 2021, and then showed significant volatility between 2022 and 2025.

Furthermore, if raw material costs decline, the resulting reduction in steel production costs would not be immediately reflected in Ternium’s operating results as we would first consume existing inventories acquired prior to such raw material cost decrease (first in - first out accounting methodology).
Similarly, we may be unable to recover, in whole or in part, increased costs of raw materials and energy through increased selling prices on steel products, or it may take considerable time to do so.
Ongoing geopolitical tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel present significant risks to the global economy.
Escalation of this conflict could disrupt energy markets and increase raw material costs.

competitive_position.claim: Trade restrictions, sanctions, or tariffs affecting heavy-equipment suppliers could delay shipments or raise equipment costs for Ternium's new Pesquería steel slab facility expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.
quotes: The imposition of government requirements, sanctions or tariffs as a result of trade or other geopolitical conflicts may prevent some of our suppliers of heavy equipment from shipping the equipment, or may result in shipping delays, or may limit our purchases or payments of products to such suppliers, and we may not be able to promptly procure such equipment from an alternative facility of such supplier or from other suppliers, or we may be required to purchase equipment at increased prices, which could result in increased expenses and/or a delayed execution of our growth plans, adversely affecting Ternium’s profitability and net worth.

competitive_position.claim: Minority shareholders in subsidiaries and associates may hinder full strategic integration, and Ternium faces a Brazilian litigation contingency from its 2012 Usiminas stake acquisition with potentially payable amounts of approximately BRL 2,369.0 million ($ 457.2 million) for Ternium Investments and BRL 838.7 million ($ 161.9 million) for Ternium Argentina as of September 30, 2026.
quotes: Finally, the existence of other minority shareholders at any acquired company, could delay or prevent us from completing our strategy or fully maximizing our combined competitive strengths.
The entities named in the CSN lawsuit had acquired participations in Usiminas in January 2012.

Based on such SCJ decision, assuming monetary adjustment through September 30, 2026, and attorney’s fees in the amount of BRL 5 million, the aggregate amount potentially payable by Ternium Investments and Ternium Argentina if CSN finally prevails on its claims would be of approximately BRL 2,369.0 million (BRL 2,143.9 million as of December 31, 2025) and BRL 838.7 million (BRL 759.0 million as of December 31, 2025).

The foregoing amounts, if the BRL/$ rate as of September 30, 2026, is used, are equivalent to approximately $ 457.2 million ($ 389.6 million as of December 31, 2025, if the BRL/$ rate as of such date is used) and $ 161.9 million ($ 138.0 million as of December 31, 2025, if the BRL/$ rate as of such date is used).
